uncited: By aligning the discrete Gaussian representation with continuous geometric priors (such as SDFs, depth maps, or explicit meshes), these methods enforce positional and normal consistency to enable accurate mesh extraction, physically-based rendering, and robust initialization [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].

Unlike sibling methods that may rely solely on photometric loss or implicit constraints, this family explicitly integrates geometric supervision into the training or post-processing pipeline to ensure the Gaussians conform to physical surfaces [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].
All methods in this family share the goal of aligning the discrete Gaussian representation with a continuous geometric prior.
The core mechanism involves adding geometric loss terms to the standard photometric rendering loss $\mathcal{L}_{rgb}$.

**Positional Consistency:** Gaussian centers $\mathbf{c}_i$ are encouraged to lie on the zero-level set of a distance function (SDF or UDF) or align with metric depth estimates [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].

**Normal Consistency:** The orientation of the Gaussians (derived from their covariance matrix or rotation quaternion) is aligned with the surface normal estimated from the geometric prior [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].
where $\mathcal{L}_{geo}$ is the geometric consistency loss and $\mathcal{L}_{norm}$ is the normal consistency loss [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].
The weights $\lambda_{geo}$ and $\lambda_{norm}$ are hyperparameters that balance photometric fidelity against geometric accuracy [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md].
More recently, diffusion-based priors (Joint 2D and 3D Priors) have been introduced to leverage large-scale generative models for geometric regularization [20090-joint-2d-and-3d-priors.md].
